summary: Import-time native-binary dropper in dependency-confusion package
details: accounts-timeline@9.6.11 presents a no-op AccountsTimeline class as its advertised API while index.js requires./setup, which schedules bootstrap() via process.nextTick on every require of the package. bootstrap() detects OS/arch, selects a per-platform asset path (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe) and invokes lib/telemetry.js run(), which fetches the payload from split-string-obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, with a *.dl.well1.site fallback), base64-decodes the response, writes it to /var/tmp or %TEMP%, chmods it 0755 and executes it via child_process. Dangerous APIs and hostnames are split across concatenated string fragments (require("child_"+"process"), fs["chmod"+"Sync"], os["plat"+"form"](), ["oob-wor","ker.cf",...].join("")) to evade pattern scanners. An installFingerprint() over hostname, username, cwd, Node version and pid is transmitted with the fetch request, identifying the installer to the operator before code execution. The package.json describes it as an SDK for 'internal consumers' at an inflated 9.6.11 version — the shape of a dependency-confusion lure targeting a private internal package name on the public npm registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
